questions.question: Which of the following countries hosted the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation in November 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Malaysia.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] In News__**

__
 
• **Malaysia hosted the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation in November 2020.**
 
• The 2020 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting was held under the **Chairmanship of Malaysian Prime Minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin.**
 
• This was the first time that all 21 APEC Economic Leaders met virtually due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The APEC 2020 ended with the adoption of the APEC Putrajaya Vision 2040 and the 2020 Kuala Lumpur Declaration.
 
• The APEC Summit 2021 will be hosted by New Zealand. This is Malaysia's second time hosting an APEC summit; the first was in 1998.
 
• The theme of the APEC Malaysia 2020 was “Optimising Human Potential Towards a Resilient Future of Shared Prosperity: Pivot. Prioritise. Progress”.
 
• The Putrajaya Vision 2040 is a new 20-year growth vision, which will replace the existing Bogor Goals, which was agreed by leaders in 1994 for free and open trade and investment in APEC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__ Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation __

 
• The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) is a regional economic forum** established in 1989 **to leverage the growing interdependence of the Asia-Pacific.
 
• APEC's 21 members aim to create greater prosperity for the people of the region by** promoting balanced, inclusive, sustainable, innovative and secure growth and by accelerating regional economic integration.**
 
• APEC has 21 members.
 
• The word "economies" is used to describe APEC members because the APEC cooperative process is predominantly concerned with trade and economic issues, with members engaging with one another as economic entities.

questions.question: Under the ______ system of land revenue, the ownership rights were handed over to the peasants and the British Government collected taxes directly from them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ryotwari.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Under the Ryotwari system of land revenue, the ownership rights were handed over to the peasants and the British government collected taxes directly from them.**
 
• At the end of the 18th century, **Captain Alexander Read and Sir Thomas Munro** developed a system that later came to be known as the Ryotwari System. Sir Thomas Munro then implemented it while serving as governor of the** Madras Presidency (1819–26)**. Under the Ryotwari system, the land revenue was paid by the farmers directly to the state.
 
• In this system, an individual cultivator by the** name of Ryot** had complete rights over the purchase, transfer, and leasing of land.
 
• The ryots could not be evicted from their land as long as they paid the rent.
 
• It was** prevalent in most of southern India, first introduced in Tamil Nadu.**
 
• Later, it was extended to Assam, Berar, East Punjab, Coorg, and Maharashtra.
 
• The advantages of this system were the elimination of middlemen, who often oppressed villagers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahalwari System**

 
 
• In **1822**, Englishman Holt Mackenzie introduced a new system known as the Mahalwari System in the North Western Provinces of the Bengal Presidency **(most of this area is now in Uttar Pradesh).**
 
• **Lord William Bentick **popularized the system in Agra and Awadh before expanding it to Madhya Pradesh and Punjab.
 
 
 
• **Malguzari System**
 
 
• The land tenure triumphing withinside the erstwhile Central Provinces changed into referred to as** Malguzari device** wherein the Malguzar changed into simply a sales farmer below the Marathas.
 
• Under the Malguzari system, the Lambardar/Sadar Lambardar appointed from amongst the Malguzars, was once the income engager.
 
 
 
• **Taluqdar System**
 
 
• The time period ‘**taluqdar**’ has unique meanings in exceptional components of India. In Oudh, taluqdar is a extraordinary landholder.
 
• But in Bengal, a taluqdar is subsequent to zamindar in extent of land manage and social status.
 
• The large zamindars themselves had created many taluqs underneath countless denominations, such as, junglburi taluq, mazkuri taluq, shikimi taluq, and so on.

questions.question: Which of the following is another name for Vitamin K1?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Phylloquinone.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phylloquinone is another name for Vitamin K1.**
 
• **Vitamin K1 is a fat soluble vitamin used to treat hemorrhagic conditions in infants and coumarin overdoses.**
 
• Vitamin K1, also called phylloquinone or phytonadione, is a** fat soluble vitamin.**
 
• Phylloquinone is a cofactor of the enzyme γ-carboxylase, which modifies and activates precursors to coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X.
 
• It is indicated in the treatment of coagulation disorders due to faulty formation of coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X caused by deficiency or interference in the activity of vitamin K.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__** Nicotinic acid**__

__
 
• Niacin, also known as nicotinic acid and vitamin B3, is a water soluble, essential B vitamin that, when given in high doses, is effective in lowering low density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and raising high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, which makes this agent of unique value in the therapy of dyslipidemia.
 
• Niacin can cause mild-to-moderate serum aminotransferase elevations and high doses and certain formulations of niacin have been linked to clinically apparent, acute liver injury which can be severe as well as fatal.

**Thiamine**__

__
 
• Thiamin (thiamine), or vitamin B1, is a water-soluble vitamin found naturally in some foods, added to foods, and sold as a supplement. Thiamin plays a vital role in the growth and function of various cells.
 
• Only small amounts are stored in the liver, so a daily intake of thiamin-rich foods is needed.

**Riboflavin**__

 
• Vitamin B2, or riboflavin, is naturally present in foods, added to foods, and available as a supplement. Bacteria in the gut can produce small amounts of riboflavin, but not enough to meet dietary needs.
 
• Riboflavin is a key component of coenzymes involved with the growth of cells, energy production, and the breakdown of fats, steroids, and medications.

questions.question: The highest peak in the Aravalli range is located in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Rajasthan.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The highest peak in the Aravalli range is located in Rajasthan.**
 
• Guru Sikhar (1,722 m), the highest peak, is situated in Mt. Abu located in Rajasthan.
 
• Aravalli range are aligned in** north-east to south-west direction.**
 
• Aravalli range run for about** 800 km between Delhi and Palanpur in Gujarat.**
 
• Aravalli range** ****one of the oldest (very old) fold mountains of the world and the oldest in India.**
 
• Now they are relict (remnants after severe weathering and erosion since millions of years) of the world’s oldest mountain formed as a result of folding (Archaean Era).
 
• They continue up to** Haridwar buried under the alluvium of Ganga Plains.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The range is conspicuous in Rajasthan (continuous range south of Ajmer where it rises to 900 m.) but becomes less distinct in Haryana and Delhi (characterized by a chain of detached and discontinuous ridges beyond Ajmer).
 
• According to some geographers, one Branch of the Aravalis extends to the Lakshadweep Archipelago through the Gulf of Khambhat and the other into Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
 
• It’s general elevation is only** 400-600 m, with few hills well above 1,000 m.**
 
• At the southwest extremity, the range rises to over 1,000 m..
 
• Here Mt. Abu (1,158 m), a small hilly block, is separated from the main range by the valley of the Banas.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Emperor Ashoka is FALSE?

options.text: Ashoka was opposed by a wise man named Chanakya (also known as Kautilya).
Ashoka belonged to the Mauryan dynasty.
The empire that Ashoka ruled was founded by his grandfather.
Ashoka is the only king in the history of the world who gave up conquest after winning a war.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka was opposed by a wise man named Chanakya (also known as Kautilya). **__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka was not opposed by a wise man named Chanakya (also known as Kautilya). **
 
• Ashoka belonged to the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• The empire that Ashoka ruled was founded by his grandfather.
 
• Ashoka is the only king in the history of the world who gave up conquest after winning a war.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**Facts about Ashoka**__

 
• **In 304 BCE**,** Bindusara and Maharani Dharma** or Shubhadrangi gave birth to **Ashoka in Patliputra.**
 
• He was known as **Samraat Chakravartin, Devanampriya, and Priyadarsin.**
 
• From the Hindu Kush Mountains in Afghanistan to Bangladesh, and from Assam in the east to Kerala and Andhra Pradesh in the south, he was in charge of a vast landmass. He died in 232 BCE. King Ashoka had an important role in Indian history and culture. 
 
• In Sanskrit, the word** "Ashoka" means "without sorrow." **The grandfather of Ashoka was the founder of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• According to the Tibetan writer Taranatha, Ashoka murdered his six brothers to seize the throne of Magadha.
 
• Ashoka was also known a**s "Chandaashoka". **
 
• Ashoka became a follower o**f Buddha after the war of Kalinga in BC 261.**
 
• He made Buddhism his state religion.
 
• He was appointed as the** "Dharma Mahapatro’** to spread Buddhism all over Asia.
 
• He sent his daughter Sanghamitra and son Mahinda to Ceylon to propagate Buddhism.
 
• He built the **lion stambh's-Ashok Stambh to spread Buddhism. **
 
• The Ashok Stambh of Sarnath was accepted as the** national emblem of India.**
 
• Apart from Ashoka Stambh, Ashoka had built many pillars, rock edicts like Bharhut stupa, Dhamek Stupa, and Mahabodhi Temple.

questions.question: In September 2021, Coal India Ltd. started a pilot project to replace the use of diesel with ______ in dumpers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** liquefied natural gas (LNG).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **In September 2021, Coal India Ltd. started a pilot project to replace use of diesel with liquefied natural gas (LNG) in dumpers.**
 
• n a big push to reduce its carbon footprint, the national miner Coal India Ltd (CIL) has initiated the process of retrofitting Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) kits in its dumpers - the big trucks engaged in the transportation of coal in mines.
 
• This is significant as the** world’s largest coal miner uses over 4 lakh kilolitres of diesel per annum with an annual expense of over Rs 3,500 crore.**
 
• The move will reduce carbon emissions significantly and also save around** Rs 500 **crore annually if all existing Heavy Earth Moving Machines (HEMMs) including dumpers are retrofitted with LNG kit.
 
• Getting rid of diesel pilferages and adulteration are other added advantages.

questions.question: In September 2021, ______ became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympic medals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Avani Lekhara.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **In September 2021, Avani Lekhara became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympic medals.** 
 
• Avani Lekhara, a para shooter, made history by becoming the** first Indian woman** to take home two medals from the Paralympics.
 
• The 19-year-old rifle shooter now has a bronze medal in the **women's 50m rifle 3-position SH1 event after winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle shooting SH1 class in Tokyo.**
 
• She also became the** first Indian woman to win two medals at the Para Games in the same edition**. After qualifying for the final in the second position with 1176 points, Avani Lekhara continued her momentum in the medal round as well.
 
• The Jaipur-based shooter, who suffered spinal cord injuries in a car accident in 2012, had fired a total of 249.6 shots, which was a new Paralympic record and tied the world record.
 
• Prior to her, **Joginder Singh Sodhi** was the lone Indian to win multiple medals in the same edition of the Games when he fetched one silver and two bronze medals in the 1984 Paralympics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Bhavina Patel
 Bhavina Hasmukhbhai Patel is an Indian parathlete and table tennis player from Mehsana, Gujarat. At the Tokyo 2020 Summer Paralympics, she took home a silver medal in Class 4 Table Tennis.
 
 

 Ekta Bhyan
 Ekta Bhyan is a para athlete who represents India in the women's club and discus throw events. She competed on behalf of her country at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, Indonesia, where she won the club throw gold medal.
 
 

 Deepa Malik
 Deepa Malik is an Indian athlete. She started her career at the age of 30. She won a silver medal in the shot put event at the 2016 Summer Paralympics, becoming the first Indian woman to do so. At the 2018 paralympic Grand Prix in Dubai, she also took home gold in the F-53/54 Javelin competition.

questions.question: The Zika virus disease is caused by a virus transmitted primarily by the ______ species of mosquitoes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aedes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Zika virus disease is caused by a virus transmitted primarily by the aedes species of mosquitoes. **
 
• Zika virus disease is caused by a** virus transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes, which bite during the day**.
 
• **Symptoms** are generally mild and include fever, rash, conjunctivitis, muscle and joint pain, malaise or headache.
 
• Symptoms typically last for 2–7 days. Most people with Zika virus infection do not develop symptoms.
 
• Zika virus infection during **pregnancy** can cause infants to be born with microcephaly and other congenital malformations, known as congenital Zika syndrome.
 
• Infection with Zika virus is also associated with other complications of pregnancy including preterm birth and miscarriage.
 
• An increased risk of neurologic complications is associated with Zika virus infection in adults and children, including Guillain-Barré syndrome, neuropathy and myelitis.

questions.question: Which of the following is a ferrous mineral?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manganese.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Manganese is a ferrous mineral.**
 
• ** Manganese is a common ferrous metal with atomic number of 25 and the chemical symbol Mn.**
 
• It constitutes roughly **0.1 per cent of the Earth’s crus**t, making it the** 12th most abundant element.**
 
• Its early uses were limited largely to pigments and oxidants in chemical processes and experiments, but the significance of manganese to human societies exploded with the development of modern steelmaking technology in the 1860s.
 
• Because manganese is essential and irreplaceable in steelmaking and its global mining industry is dominated by just a few nations, it is considered one of the most critical mineral commodities for the United States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The metals other than** iron and alloys that do not contain an appreciable amount of ferrous (iron) are known as non-ferrous metals. A distinguishing feature of non-ferrous metals is that they are highly malleable (i.e., they can be pressed or hammered into thin sheets without breaking). **
 
• Nonferrous metallic minerals include metals such as **copper, nickel, platinum, palladium, gold, silver, cobalt, chromium, zinc, lead, bismuth, tin, tungsten, tantalum, or niobium. **

questions.question: In June 2021, the Ministry of Heavy Industries increased the subsidy for electric two-wheelers to ______ per kWh under the FAME India Scheme Phase II.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ₹15,000.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Under the FAME India Scheme Phase II, the Ministry of Heavy Industries increased the subsidy for electric two-wheelers to 15,000 per kWh in June 2021.**
 
• The Central government has increased the subsidy under the** second phase of the FAME India scheme on electric two-wheelers by 50 percent.**
 
• The subsidy will now be** Rs 15,000 per kWh for electric two-wheelers under FAME India phase II.** Earlier, it was Rs 10,000 per kWh. In addition, the maximum subsidy for an electric two-wheeler will now be 40% of its cost, up from 20% previously.
 
• The government's continued support of electronic vehicles (EVs) will lower the price of electric two-wheelers, which will be very advantageous to buyers of electric motorcycles and scooters.
 
• Future mobility options must be sustainable, and better incentives for electric two-wheelers will boost adoption and encourage additional domestic technological investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Some of the key features of the FAME II scheme are given below.**

 
 
• Allocation of Rs 10,000 crores for a period of 3 years from 2019 to 2022. A budget of Rs 1 billion crore has been set aside to install electric vehicle charging stations.
 
• It has been suggested that every electric bus receive one slow charging unit and every ten electric buses receive one fast charging station.
 
• The purchase of about 5 lakh three-wheelers, 7000 electric buses, and 35,000 four-wheelers will be encouraged by the central government.
 
• FAME India Scheme's official website is located at https://fame2.heavyindustry.gov.in/. The Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises is in charge of overseeing the program.

questions.question: Jawai Bandh is a reservoir built across Jawai River, which is a tributary of the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Luni river.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawai Bandh is a reservoir built across Jawai River, which is a tributary of the Luni river.**
 
• The dam is near** Sumerpur town in Pali District of Rajasthan state in India.**
 
• The dam was built by **Maharaja Umaid Singh of Jodhpur. he gave idea of building a dam over River.**
 
• Jawai w conceived in 1903 as its flooding waters caused heavy damage in Pali and Jalore district during monsoon. It was finally given shape in 1946.
 
• This dam covers an** area of 13 km2**.
 
• This is the biggest man-made dam in **western Rajasthan.**
 
• The dam has a capacity of 7887.5 million cubic feet and covers an area of 102,315 acres (414.05 km2) of cultivable command area. Its height is about 61.25 feet (18.67 m).
 
• Sei dam and Kalibor dam are the feeder dams of the Jawai dam. The catchment area of the dam site is 720 square kilometres and the basin is in the shape of a fan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Banas river**
 Banas River, river in Rajasthan state, northwestern India. It rises near Kumbhalgarh and cuts its way tortuously through the Aravalli Range.
 
 

 **Chambal river**
 Chambal River, river, northern India. The Chambal is the chief tributary of the Yamuna River and rises in the Vindhya Range just south of Mhow, western Madhya Pradesh state
 
 

 **Mahi river**
 Mahi River, a stream in western India. It rises in the western Vindhya Range, just south of Sardarpur, and flows northward through Madhya Pradesh state.

questions.question: 6 April 1919 was observed as a day of non-violent opposition to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** The Rowlatt Act.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **6 April 1919 was observed as a day of non-violent opposition to the Rowlatt Act.**
 
• On 6 April 1919, Mahatma Gandhi started a non-violent Satyagraha against the unjust Rowlatt Act passed by the British government.
 
• The Rowlatt Act was the popular name for the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919 passed by the British Indian government.**
 
• This Act was termed the** ‘Black Act’ **by the Indian public because of its unjust and restrictive nature. The Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council on 18th March 1919.
 
• It basically extended the **emergency provisions imposed by the 1915 Defence of India Act **that was passed during the First World War.
 
• The Act gave the **government the power to imprison any person suspected of terrorist activities for a maximum period of two years without trial.**
 
• This was known as the** Rowlatt Satyagraha and April 6th was the designated date for the hartal to begin**. People would refrain from going to work and hold meetings against the repressive act.
 
• The government clamped down heavily on the people. There were violent clashes in many parts.
 
• Two Congress leaders** Dr. Satya Pal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew were arrested**. The army was deployed in Punjab where martial law was enacted.
 
• The** infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in Amritsar on 13th April 1919. **The people had gathered at the enclosed garden to celebrate Baisakhi and also to condemn the arrest of the two leaders.
 
• C**olonel Reginald Dyer **arrived there with his troops and without warning fired upon the unarmed crowd.
 
• **In March 1922, the Rowlatt Act and 22 other acts were repealed by the government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**The Simon Commission**__

__
 
• Simon Commission was the Indian Statutory Commission, which was a group of seven Members of Parliament under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon.
 
• The commission arrived in British India in 1928 to study constitutional reform in Britain’s largest and most important possession.
 
• The Government of India Act of 1919 provided for the appointment of a commission to study the progress of the governance scheme and suggest new steps after ten years Since the British administration had failed to include even a single Indian in the Commission, it was strongly opposed by national leaders and freedom.

**The Cabinet Mission Plan**__

__
 
• Cabinet Mission was a high-powered mission sent in February 1946 to India by the Atlee Government (British Prime Minister.) The mission had three British cabinet members – Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, & and A.V. Alexander.
 
• The Cabinet Mission’s aim was to discuss the transfer of power from British to Indian leadership.
 
• **Objectives of Cabinet Mission** -To obtain an agreement with the Indian leaders as to the framing of a constitution for India.
 
• To formulate a constitution-making body (the Constituent Assembly of India)
 
• To establish an Executive Council with the support of the major Indian parties.

**The Morely-Minto Reforms**__

 
• The Indian Councils Act 1909 was an act of the British Parliament that introduced a few reforms in the legislative councils and increased the involvement of Indians (limited) in the governance of British India.
 
• It was more commonly called the Morley-Minto Reforms after the Secretary of State for India John Morley and the Viceroy of India, the 4th Earl of Minto
 
• The legislative councils at the Centre and the provinces increased in size.
 
• Indians were given membership to the Imperial Legislative Council for the first time.
 
• It introduced separate electorates for the Muslims. 
 
• The members could discuss the budget and move resolutions. They could also discuss matters of public interest.
 
• They could also ask supplementary questions. No discussions on foreign policy or on relations with the princely states were permitted.
 
• Lord Minto appointed (on much persuasion by Morley) Satyendra P Sinha as the first Indian member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.
 
• Two Indians were nominated to the Council of the Secretary of State for Indian affairs.

questions.question: In which year was the Oudh Kisan Sabha set up?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1920.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oudh Kisan Sabha was set up in 1920.**
 
• **Oudh Kisan Sabha, also known as Awadh Kisan Sabha, was formed by Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramachandra and others.**
 
• It was formed to fight against the **landlords and talukdars, who demanded exorbitant taxes and rents.**
 
• After the 1857 revolt, the Awadh taluqdars had got back their lands.
 
• This strengthened the hold of the taluqdars or big landlords over the agrarian society of the province.
 
• The majority of the cultivators were subjected to high rents, summary evictions (**bedakhali**), illegal levies, renewal fees or nazrana.
 
• The First World War had hiked the prices of food and other necessities.
 
• This worsened the conditions of the UP peasants. Mainly due to the efforts of the Home Rule activists, Kisan sabhas were organised in UP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The United Provinces Kisan Sabha was set up in February 1918 by Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi. Madan Mohan Malaviya supported their efforts. By June 1919, the UP Kisan Sabha had 450 branches.**
 
• Other prominent leaders included **Jhinguri Singh, Durgapal Singh and Baba Ramchandra.**
 
• In June 1920, Baba Ramchandra urged Nehru to visit these villages. During these visits, Nehru developed close contacts with the villagers.
 
• In** October 1920, the Awadh Kisan Sabha came into existence because of differences in nationalist ranks.**

questions.question: What is the maximum amount of loan permissible under the ‘Shishu scheme’ of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ₹50,000.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **₹50,000 maximum amount of loan permissible under the ‘Shishu scheme’ of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana.**
 
• Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency Ltd. [MUDRA] is an NBFC supporting development of micro enterprise sector in the country.
 
• MUDRA provides refinance support to Banks / MFIs / NBFCs for lending to micro units having loan requirement upto 10 lakh.
 
• MUDRA provides refinance support to micro business under the Scheme of Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana
 
• . The other products are for development support to the sector.
 
• The bouquet of offerings of MUDRA is depicted below.
 
• The offerings are being targeted across the spectrum of beneficiary segments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__** Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana**__

 
• Under the aegis of Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), MUDRA has created products/ schemes.
 
• The interventions have been named 'Shishu', 'Kishore' and 'Tarun' to signify the stage of growth / development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro unit / entrepreneur and also provide a reference point for the next phase of graduation / growth to look forward to :
 
• **Shishu : covering loans upto 50,000/- **
 
• **Kishor : covering loans above 50,000/- and upto 5 lakh**
 
• **Tarun : covering loans above 5 lakh and upto 10 lakh.**
 
• With an objective to promote entrepreneurship among the new generation aspiring youth, it is ensured that more focus is given to Shishu Category Units and then Kishore and Tarun categories.
 
• Within the framework and overall objective of development and growth of micro enterprises sector under Shishu, Kishore and Tarun, the products being offered by MUDRA are so designed, to meet requirements of different sectors / business activities as well as business/ entrepreneur segments.
 
• The funding support from MUDRA are of two types: Micro Credit Scheme (MCS) for loans up to 1 lakh finance through MFIs.
 
• Refinance Scheme for Commercial Banks / Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) / Small Finance Banks / Non Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).
